text: For each player, choose target nonenchantment, nonland permanent that player controls. Those permanents' owners shuffle them into their libraries. Each player who controlled one of those permanents exiles cards from the top of their library until they exile a nonland card, then puts the rest on the bottom of their library in a random order. Each player may cast the nonland card they exiled without paying its mana cost.
failing_piece: Those permanents' owners shuffle them into their libraries.
note: drilled: "The owners of those permanents shuffle them into their libraries" compiles (C6-g-4) and "Shuffle those permanents into their owners' libraries" compiles (C6-g-1), the possessive subject "Those permanents' owners" fails (autoprobe); "Each player exiles cards from the top of their library until they exile a nonland card, then puts the rest on the bottom ... in a random order" compiles (C6-g-5), "Each player who controlled one of those permanents" as its subject fails (C6-g-2, C6-g-7 with a plain draw: a player filter over the controllers, last known, of a set the effect moved; Infernal Offering's "Each player who sacrificed a creature this way" compiles); third piece: "Each player may cast the nonland card they exiled without paying its mana cost" fails (C6-g-3, C6-g-6, C6-g-8), and so does Rocco's own "each player may play the card they exiled this way" under "Until end of turn" (C6-gu-9; Rocco, Street Chef compiles in its exact form): each player's own result of a per-player reveal-until as "the card they exiled".

text: When ~ enters, each opponent may search their library for up to three basic land cards. They each put one of those cards onto the battlefield tapped under your control and the rest onto the battlefield tapped under their control. Then each player who searched their library this way shuffles.
failing_piece: They each put one of those cards onto the battlefield tapped under your control and the rest onto the battlefield tapped under their control.
note: drilled: each opponent's search with every found card put under your control (C6-rw-1, C6-rw-3, C6-rw-9) or under their control (C6-rw-8) compiles, with "Then each player who searched their library this way shuffles" (C6-rw-1); splitting each searcher's found cards between two destinations fails in every form (C6-rw-2, C6-rw-4 "They each put those cards", C6-rw-5 with one target opponent, C6-rw-7 "and the rest into their hand"), while the controller's own split compiles (C6-rw-6; Verdant Mastery "Put two of them onto the battlefield tapped under your control and the rest into your hand"): a split of a per-player found set, done by each searching player in APNAP order (ruling: the next opponent in turn order decides first; with one card found it goes under your control).

text: At the beginning of each upkeep, each player exiles the top card of their library. The player who exiled the card with the greatest mana value takes an extra turn after this one. If two or more players' cards are tied for greatest, the tied players repeat this process until the tie is broken.
failing_piece: The player who exiled the card with the greatest mana value takes an extra turn after this one.
note: drilled: "each player exiles the top card of their library" compiles; "The player who exiled [reveals] the card with the greatest mana value" fails with any body, exiled or revealed, past or present (C6-ts-1, C6-ts-2, C6-ts-3, C6-ts-4, C6-ts-5, C6-ts-6, C6-ts-8, and "Each player who revealed ..." C6-ts-9), although Psychic Battle ("The player who reveals the card with the greatest mana value may change the target or targets") and Goblin Game ("The player who revealed the fewest items") compile: the comparison over each player's result exists, the grammar takes only those bodies. Second piece: "If two or more players' cards are tied for greatest, the tied players repeat this process until the tie is broken" fails (C6-ts-7): a repeat of the per-player step among the tied players (rulings: only the players in the tie continue; a player who exiles no card can't take the turn). The tie loop is unique to Timesifter (search "tied players|repeat this process until the tie"), but it is the tie rule of the shared comparison: build it with the comparison in repeat_process.rs; if it can't be expressed, report it as a manual candidate rather than hand-writing the whole card.

text: At the beginning of your upkeep, secretly choose a number between N and N that hasn't been chosen. If you do, an opponent guesses which number you chose, then you reveal the number you chose. If they guessed wrong, they lose life equal to the number they guessed and you draw a card. If they guessed right, sacrifice ~.
failing_piece: secretly choose a number between 1 and 5 that hasn't been chosen.
note: drilled: "secretly choose a number between 1 and 5" compiles (C6-toy-3); "that hasn't been chosen" fails, secret or not (C6-toy-2, C6-toy-6): numbers chosen for this object before, remembered per object (ruling: a new object has no memory), the construct of the modal "choose one that hasn't been chosen" (Demonic Pact, Sol'Kanar the Tainted, Three Bowls of Porridge, Silent Hallcreeper; compiled) and Long List of the Ents' "hasn't been noted for ~" (compiled) applied to a number choice. Second piece: "an opponent guesses which number you chose, then you reveal the number you chose" fails (C6-toy-1, C6-toy-4, C6-toy-5, C6-toy-7), while guesses of a yes/no question compile (Liar's Pendulum, Master of Predicaments, Gollum, Scheming Guide, The Seventh Doctor): a guess of a value by another player (a decision routed to the opponent), then "If they guessed wrong, they lose life equal to the number they guessed"; C6-toy-8 shows "an opponent loses life equal to that number" after a plain choice also fails.

text: Look at the top five cards of your library. As many times as you choose, you may pay N life, put those cards on the bottom of your library in any order, then look at the top five cards of your library. Then shuffle and put the last cards you looked at this way on top in any order.
failing_piece: As many times as you choose, you may pay 1 life, put those cards on the bottom of your library in any order, then look at the top five cards of your library.
note: drilled: Dance with Calamity's "As many times as you choose, you may exile the top card of your library" compiles (C6-lim-5), the loop with a payment fails (C6-lim-1, C6-lim-4, C6-lim-6) and so does Lim-Dûl's body without the payment (C6-lim-7: put the looked-at cards on the bottom, then look again): the optional repeat with a per-iteration cost and a multi-step body over "those cards" (repeat_process.rs). Second piece: "Then shuffle and put the last cards you looked at this way on top in any order" fails (C6-lim-2) and so does "Then shuffle and put those cards on top in any order" (C6-lim-8): shuffle the rest of the library, then put the last looked-at set back on top (rulings: with no life paid the five go back on top after the shuffle; with five or fewer cards you see the same cards). "the last cards you looked at this way" is the loop's last iteration's set: a referent of the shared loop, not a one-off (search: only Lim-Dûl's Vault and Dance with Calamity use "As many times as you choose").
